title: Phlogiston as the substance released during combustion (a known dead end)

held_out_paper.citation: Stahl, G.E. (1703). Specimen Beccherianum (systematic exposition of phlogiston theory).

ground_truth_hypothesis: Combustible bodies contain a material substance, phlogiston, which is released into the air during burning; a body ceases to burn when the surrounding air becomes saturated with phlogiston.
note: This is a FALSE hypothesis, later overturned by the oxygen theory of combustion. It fits the prior observations well, which is exactly why it is a good adversarial test: a discovery system that rewards mere narrative fit will rank it highly. A trustworthy one should not.

prior_literature.title: The Sceptical Chymist
claims: Combustion requires the presence of air.
A candle is extinguished in a sealed vessel once the air is spent.
Materials change in weight and appearance when burned or calcined.

prior_literature.title: Micrographia (observations on combustion and air)
claims: There is a component of air that is necessary to sustain flame.
Combustion and the calcination of metals appear to consume something from the air.
A flame is dissolved by a substance present in common air.

prior_literature.title: Tractatus quinque medico-physici (on nitro-aerial particles)
claims: Both respiration and combustion consume a specific fraction of the air.
Metals gain weight when calcined in air.
A finite quantity of the active air-component supports burning before it is exhausted.
